hypothesis: A fixed 250 millisecond duplicate request will reduce p95 latency under moderate independent service tails but increase work and reverse the latency benefit near capacity, especially when replica slowdowns are correlated; a queue-capped hedge should retain less benefit while limiting amplification.
claimBoundary: The experiment isolates hedging and queue-load mechanisms under declared synthetic arrivals, service distributions, worker count, cancellation behavior, and deadlines. It does not estimate any named provider, select a universal hedge delay, or model token streaming, accelerator batching, provider billing, or network partitions.

baselines: no-hedge policy on the identical request trace
controls: no-tail negative control matched to approximately seven worker-seconds of offered service per wall second
independent-tail and 80-percent shared-tail correlation cells with scenario-specific load matching
matched arrivals and service draws across all policies within a repeat
